newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen futures end down but off earlier low.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen futures end down but off earlier low.

text.p: May 9 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (Z) 98.86 98.92
Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures ended Friday's TIFFE day session down but off earlier lows.

The benchmark contract fell as low as 98.82 in the morning on worries over a possible interest rate rise, but pared losses in the afternoon as Japanese government bond futures bounced back from earlier lows.
Day session turnover for the December was 138,044 lots.
"Short-covering emerged in the afternoon as JGB futures cut part of their losses while Tokyo stocks extended their losses," said a brokerage house trader.
Key June JGB futures ended down 0.60 at 123.45, but well off their intraday low of 122.70. The Nikkei 225 stock average ended down 259.03 points, or 1.29 percent, at 19,802.78.
"Some players squared their short positions to take profits before the weekend," said a city bank trader.
Traders said heavy selling was seen in the morning as the mood soured after a senior Finance Ministry official said on Thursday that the yen may strengthen to 103 yen to the dollar.

The remarks by Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of MOF's international finance bureau, led to speculation that MOF would be willing to see an interest rate rise to prevent the yen from weakening further, traders said.
Some foreign players were on the selling side this morning, a trust bank trader said.
Traders, however, said the December may have hit the near-term bottom at 98.82.
"We could say that the December has already factored in a credit tightening by the Bank of Japan. So it is likely to be supported at around 98.80," said the brokerage house trader.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was mainly traded at 0.46 percent, down from Thursday's weighted average of 0.49 percent, traders said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) drained a net 200 billion yen in its regular money market operation, leaving the market in surplus by about 120 billion yen.
Money traders said the overnight rate had been expected to fall on Friday due to weekend factors.
About 60 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.58 percent, up from Thursday's 0.57 percent.
About 15 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.55 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
Interest rate swap (IRS) rates were up but off earlier highs as JGBs pared losses in the afternoon, traders said.
Five-year IRS rates were quoted at 2.17/2.21 percent, up from 2.10/2.14 percent late on Thursday but down compared with 2.24/2.28 percent at midday Friday.
Seven-year IRS rates were at 2.63/2.67 percent, up from the previous day's 2.56/2.60 percent, but down compared with 2.70/2.74 percent at midday.
-- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
